Pre-epoch STEREO-A and Solar Orbiter measurements over November 10–24 set instrument-balanced density, magnetic and thermal normalizations. Wind is entirely held out. The calibrated boundary uses n₄₀₀=8.25 cm⁻³ at 1 AU, T₄₀₀=9.58e+05 K at the inner boundary, and a WSA field multiplier 2.36. At native map nodes, constant momentum flux sets n∝v⁻² and constant thermal pressure sets T∝v². Independent linear interpolation of these primitive fields does not exactly preserve those nonlinear relations between nodes; that boundary-interpolation assumption is audited separately. Pressure is 2nₚkBTₚ, assuming equal electron and proton temperatures and hydrogen-only mass density. The chosen WSA-to-MHD speed reduction is 50 km/s; it is tested as an uncertain model choice, not represented as the exact ENLIL boundary transformation.

The thermodynamic interpolation audit samples the actual boundary, rather than assuming constant pressure between map nodes. Separate linear interpolation raises sampled source-band pressure by a median 0.99%, a 99th percentile 28.8%, and up to 75.7% on the combined spatial/time grid. Native-spatial-node hourly samples reach a factor 2.014; these are sampled maxima rather than analytic upper bounds. A separate optional closure interpolates speed first, then computes n=C/v² and T=Dv², with scalar normalization factors and conditional CME changes applied afterward. Its default-off control reproduces the original; 8000 CPU queries verify the enabled algebra. The new closure is a different controlled driver and must not be conflated with historical primitive-interpolated runs. Sampling details and equations; CPU control and provenance.

STEREO-A is only about 1.1° away from the comet in solar latitude; Solar Orbiter is about 15.9° away. Their training density-normalization medians differ substantially (6.05 versus 11.25 cm⁻³), motivating separate low/high-density experiments. Spacecraft normalization does not recover the neutral coma, heavy-ion charge states or a unique unobserved density map. A prior heavy-ion fraction 3×10⁻⁴–10⁻³ could be applied to proton flux conditionally, but it is not a contemporaneous heavy-ion measurement.

A second independent Athena++ benchmark propagates the actual rotating boundary with B=0, using HLLC/PLM/RK2, the same gravity and thermal closure, and exactly prescribed inner mass flux. Positivity floors are configured to abort rather than conceal failures; none activate. Its 72→96-cell refinement changes the PN-weighted incident flux by −10.47% and the local time series by up to about 24.5%. The in-house hydrodynamic LLF controls also retain substantial method dependence. Thus the outstanding transport sensitivity exists without magnetic cleaning. A smooth hot radial-wind check against the analytic Bernoulli relation gives coarse speed errors of approximately −2.47% for the in-house solver and −0.35% for Athena; these checks do not identify a major pressure-unit or gravity error. An exact magnetized expanding-wind benchmark independently tests spherical geometry. With constant radial speed, ρ∝r⁻², p∝r⁻³, Br∝r⁻², zero rotation and 3p₀r₀/ρ₀=GM, pressure balances gravity, entropy is constant for γ=1.5, and the radial field has zero curl and divergence within the shell. 3I/ATLAS solar-wind reconstruction — Codex

STATUS: completed 3D constrained-transport (CT) control runs pass the current
formulation and long-run parallel-equivalence checks. Full numerical
convergence, domain/initial-condition qualification and an explicit final CT
reference selection are still pending. These passes do not establish accuracy.
The current report.html remains provisional until selected CT products are
rendered. The earlier GLM report and its directly linked records are preserved
at report_glm_history.html and history/glm/archive_manifest.json.

The CT calculation uses pinned Athena++ native double-precision HLLD transport,
PLM reconstruction, SSPRK2, spherical geometry, gravity and staggered magnetic
CT. Our problem generator supplies the calibrated, rotating boundary, compatible
surface electric fields, physical ghost cells, probes and passive audits. Native
radial MeshBlocks/OpenMP provide CPU parallelism; CT does not use the GPU.
The pinned upstream is https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/athena at commit
e47fabb7dd5efb22e1e2c7ff193148d723e3e952. Sources, own code, compiled binaries, receipts and tests
are retained under solver/athena_ct*, solver/athena_ct_pins/ and validation/.

Work from this directory with Python 3.12 and requirements.txt installed. GCC
with OpenMP and GNU time are needed for solver builds/run accounting; ffmpeg
is needed for MP4/GIF product rendering. Frozen archived CT executables allow
replay without a new Athena checkout, /tmp build tree or network access.
Acquisition from NASA, NSO, JPL and the other cited services is documented
separately; reproduction uses the copied inputs and evidence already present.

Reproduction:

    make plan

This prints a read-only plan from results/reference_selection.json and the
selected cases' actual run.cfg, native input, code selection, input/source
hashes and runner receipts. It invents no reference, case, settings or resource
caps. It refuses a missing CT selection, missing records, changed hashes, or
configuration disagreement. required_case_names, when explicitly present in
the selection, defines the campaign; otherwise the union of the selected
reference/animation and all category_comparisons supplies its case names.

    make simulations

This explicitly executes the planned groups through the qualified archived-pin
controller. Matching completed cases are reused. To recompute the recorded
campaign, explicitly use:

    make simulations FORCE=--force

The controller archives prior outputs under each case's previous_attempts/
before recomputing. No other command silently adds --force. Per-case recorded
threads, radial blocks, resource caps, input capabilities and movie settings
are reused; incompatible cases form separate sequential groups. Each group
has at most two simultaneous jobs and eight reserved CPU threads. The shared
runner guard also enforces 3 GiB aggregate RSS, nice 15 and finite process-tree
wall/CPU/RSS/address-space limits. Actual caps and measured costs are in each
runner_usage.json and GNU-time resource_usage.txt; they vary by case.

    make all

make all and make products regenerate selected CT products through
scripts/render_products.py --gif. They require an explicit completed CT
reference and a completed selected CT animation case with recorded movie
output. No selection currently means a clear refusal, never a fallback to an
old GLM run. Products do not launch simulations, even with FORCE set. To
recompute and then render, run the two commands separately. make audit refreshes
the cached campaign diagnostics and registered convergence comparisons.
The original top-level GLM recipe is history/glm/Makefile.original; it is a
